title: Earliest evidence of land plants (Ordovician cryptospores)
summary: The oldest evidence of plants on land is a record of microscopic spores from the Ordovician. Spores from the Canning Basin in Western Australia are reported at about 480 million years old, and cryptospores from Argentina at about 473 to 471 million years. Each study presents its find as the earliest.

uncertainty.note: Range runs from the Canning Basin spores (about 480 Ma, ScienceAlert republication of a Conversation article) to the Argentine Dapingian cryptospores (473-471 Ma, Rubinstein et al. 2010). The opened pages state no error bars.

as_recorded.value: about 480 million years old (Nambeet Formation, Early Ordovician, 485 to 470 million years ago)
Dapingian, about 473-471 million years ago (early Middle Ordovician)

where.modern_name: Canning Basin, Western Australia (one of two reported sites; the other is in Argentina)
where.historical_name: Canning Basin, Ordovician; no polities exist at this date

importance.justification: Marks the earliest fossil evidence of plants on land, though the exact first appearance is disputed.
